This Anthropic harness paper is the most useful f*cking thing I've read on agents

Anthropic's Labs team gave Claude one sentence and got a full app back 6 hours later

and the model wasn't what changed

what changed: three agents, and none of them grades its own work -> that's harness engineering

prompt -> spec -> contract -> build -> QA -> fix

The 6 parts of the harness:

Part 1 -> planner

1-4 sentences go in, a 16-feature spec comes out
Product level only, no implementation details

Part 2 -> sprint contract

Before any code is written, the generator and the evaluator agree on what "done" means
They negotiate in files

Part 3 -> generator

One feature per sprint
It checks itself, then hands off to QA

Part 4 -> evaluator

Clicks through the live app with Playwright
Sprint 3 alone had 27 criteria

Part 5 -> hard thresholds

Depth, functionality, design, code
One score under the bar -> the sprint fails

Part 6 -> cost

Solo: 20 min, $9, the game ignored every input
Harness: 6 hr, $200, the game was playable

An agent grading its own work always passes. A stranger with Playwright doesn't

I packed all 6 parts into one prompt. Paste it into Claude Code and Claude builds the harness for you

3 agents, 1 prompt, 0 self-grading

Then read the article below ↓

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku and Opus 5.5 together, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Opus-level judgment on every big call, without paying Opus rates for every routine turn.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

here's the split:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session and writes the code
→ Haiku 5.5 explores files and docs in parallel
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls
→ you stop spending Opus on work that doesn't need it

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

Sonnet builds. Haiku explores. Opus reviews.

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and edits code
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5
> grep finds call sites on Haiku 5.5

> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reads the whole transcript when consulted

Simple AEO hack:

- Go to Google Analytics
- Admin > Data display > Channel groups
- Create new channel group > Add new channel
- Name it "AI Search"
- Source > matches regex > paste one of the regex below
- Move it above Referral and save

Now you can see exactly how many people ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini send you, and which pages they land on.

1. All the main AI assistants

^(.*\.)?(chatgpt\.com|chat\.openai\.com|perplexity\.ai|claude\.ai|gemini\.google\.com|copilot\.microsoft\.com|chat\.deepseek\.com|grok\.com|meta\.ai)$

2. Just ChatGPT

^(.*\.)?(chatgpt\.com|chat\.openai\.com)$

3. Just Perplexity

^(.*\.)?perplexity\.ai$

4. Everything except ChatGPT

^(.*\.)?(perplexity\.ai|claude\.ai|gemini\.google\.com|copilot\.microsoft\.com|grok\.com)$

AI Agents are much more than just LLMs.

A language model can understand and generate text, but an AI agent needs an entire architecture to reason, make decisions, use tools, and execute tasks autonomously.

Here are the 7 core components behind AI Agents.👇

1️⃣ Reasoning & Planning
↳ Break complex tasks into smaller steps.
↳ Analyze situations and decide what to do next.
↳ Plan actions to achieve specific goals.

2️⃣ Memory & Context
↳ Remember previous interactions.
↳ Maintain context across multiple tasks.
↳ Store relevant information for future decisions.

3️⃣ Orchestration
↳ Coordinate multiple agents and workflows.
↳ Manage task execution and decision-making.
↳ Connect different components into one system.

4️⃣ RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
↳ Retrieve information from external knowledge sources.
↳ Access company documents and databases.
↳ Generate context-aware and relevant responses.

5️⃣ Tools & APIs
↳ Interact with external applications.
↳ Execute code and query databases.
↳ Connect agents with real-world systems.

6️⃣ Guardrails & Evaluations
↳ Prevent unsafe or unwanted actions.
↳ Monitor accuracy and reliability.
↳ Evaluate agent performance and outputs.

7️⃣ Deployment
↳ Run agents in production environments.
↳ Monitor performance and scalability.
↳ Optimize latency, infrastructure, and costs.

The key takeaway:

An LLM provides the intelligence, but the surrounding architecture gives an AI agent the ability to plan, remember, interact, execute, and complete tasks.

The future isn't just about building more powerful AI models.

It's about building reliable, scalable, and autonomous AI systems.

That's the real foundation of Agentic AI.

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku and Opus 5.5 together, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Opus-level judgment on every big call, without paying Opus rates for every routine turn.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

here's the split:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session and writes the code
→ Haiku 5.5 explores files and docs in parallel
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls
→ you stop spending Opus on work that doesn't need it

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

outsiders.name: Marspective
outsiders.text:
The biggest shift in Web3 AI isn’t another model launch.

Over the past month, AI projects have continued building the infrastructure needed for autonomous agents to operate in the real world.

From agentic trading and AI wallets to decentralized inference, social data, compute markets and onchain execution, here’s what shipped in the last month.

—
● @AlloraNetwork
• Launched Atlas, the Allora Forge timeseries data platform for machine learning builders

• Launched inference contracts on @trondao’s Nile Testnet, bringing decentralized AI predictions onto smart contract networks

● @crossmint
• Introduced Menta, the first open-source plugin that lets AI assistants buy anything, from any store, anywhere

● @UnbrowseAI
• Released an open-source API discovery and replay engine that compiles websites into direct HTTP capabilities for AI agents

● @AIsaOneHQ
• Introduced AIsa Social, a platform and API layer that connects AI agents to public social media data, content generation tools, and authorized account management

● @InstantlyAI
• Launched PULSE-1, an AI model built for sales and GTM

● @VeniceAI
• Launched Venice Minds, a feature that lets users build customizable AI agents without coding and publish them on Mind Market

● @wirexapp
• Launched Navoka, an AI agent with its own IBAN, debit card and stablecoin wallets, with spending rules controlled by the owner

● @lightning
• Announced pi402, an open-source extension that allows AI coding agents to autonomously pay for model inference using Bitcoin over the Lightning Network

● @aqua_ai_group
• Launched Aqua AI, a personal AI agent ecosystem

● @42space
• Launched 42 Agentic Pass, an NFT that allows users to fund autonomous AI trading agents and earn Points through Agentic Mining

● @raincards
• Launched Agent Vaults, allowing AI agents to spend from owner-funded balances using controlled virtual card numbers

● @useTria
• Launched Agentic Trading, allowing users to connect AI agents to their self-custodial Tria accounts and let agents open/close perpetual positions on @HyperliquidX and @DecibelTrade

● @flop_labs
• Launched Flop Network on Testnet, an L1 and payment/compute layer for autonomous AI agents

● @Visa
• Launched an experimental AI agent wallet that allows eligible U.S. Visa users to verify agents and earn OUSD when those agents complete paid tasks

● @akashnet
• Introduced Akash Compute Forwards, a forward market for GPU-hours

● @tari
• Launched Ootle, a general-purpose L2 for dApps and private payments, with an architecture and dev tooling heavily tailored for autonomous AI workflows

● @SperaxUSD
• Launched SperaxOS, its AI agent workspace for crypto and DeFi, on @Microsoft Marketplace

● @spacexai
• Launched Grok Bot 1.0, a full-release AI agent designed to work as a proactive, multiplayer "AI teammate" across apps, websites, and team workflows

● @reya_xyz
• Launched Reya Agentic, an AI-driven trading system that designs, tests, and executes 24/7 trading strategies automatically

● @almanak
• Released Almanak SDK 3.3.0, expanding the open source Python DeFi framework to support direct, natural-language DeFi operations driven by AI agents

● @OzakAGI
• Introduced Agent Harness, the orchestration and control layer powering its autonomous financial intelligence and trading platform

● @aibtcdev
• Inbox auto-reply went live, an autonomous messaging feature that lets Bitcoin-native agents independently read, generate, sign, and respond to incoming paid messages

● @origamitech_
• Launched AI Portfolio Manager, an AI agent for automated trading that coordinates user-selected trading strategies and enforces risk rules across exchanges

● @SolanaFndn
• Launched Solana AI Hub, a centralized hub for autonomous AI agents that trade, manage wallets, access compute, and pay for online services on @solana

● @ritualnet
• Launched Ritual Chain, an EVM-compatible L1 built specifically to run AI models, external web requests, and autonomous agents directly onchain

—
That’s all for the month. Stick around for more updates across the web3 AI sector monthly.

This sh*t is wild. Claude Code clears your whole backlog while you sleep

You close the laptop at midnight.
By 7 there are PRs waiting, tests green and a report on top.

No magic. Just 6 resources most people never open:

1. Headless mode
Run Claude from a script or cron with claude -p and cap the spend with --max-budget-usd.
https://t.co/8JaBCMV68r

2. Dev containers
Lets Claude run unattended with no permission prompts, locked inside a container.
https://t.co/u6OFn8SSro

Anthropic's setup for work across many context windows: an initializer agent plus a coding agent that leaves notes for the next shift.
https://t.co/5sw2FwDCiw

An Opus 4 lead with Sonnet 4 subagents beat a single Opus 4 agent by 90.2% on their internal eval.
https://t.co/ZfotKd9izO

5. Claude Code best practices
Has a whole part on letting Claude run without you, plus /verify to check work you didn't watch.
https://t.co/7wjwFBZCqP

6. Claude Code Security Review
A GitHub Action that scans every overnight PR for vulnerabilities before you merge.
https://t.co/tJuGEdrhIc

You sleep. Claude works. You review over coffee.

outsiders.text:
AI Agents are much more than just LLMs.

A language model can understand and generate text, but an AI agent needs an entire architecture to reason, make decisions, use tools, and execute tasks autonomously.

Here are the 7 core components behind AI Agents.👇

1️⃣ Reasoning & Planning
↳ Break complex tasks into smaller steps.
↳ Analyze situations and decide what to do next.
↳ Plan actions to achieve specific goals.

2️⃣ Memory & Context
↳ Remember previous interactions.
↳ Maintain context across multiple tasks.
↳ Store relevant information for future decisions.

3️⃣ Orchestration
↳ Coordinate multiple agents and workflows.
↳ Manage task execution and decision-making.
↳ Connect different components into one system.

4️⃣ RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
↳ Retrieve information from external knowledge sources.
↳ Access company documents and databases.
↳ Generate context-aware and relevant responses.

5️⃣ Tools & APIs
↳ Interact with external applications.
↳ Execute code and query databases.
↳ Connect agents with real-world systems.

6️⃣ Guardrails & Evaluations
↳ Prevent unsafe or unwanted actions.
↳ Monitor accuracy and reliability.
↳ Evaluate agent performance and outputs.

7️⃣ Deployment
↳ Run agents in production environments.
↳ Monitor performance and scalability.
↳ Optimize latency, infrastructure, and costs.

The key takeaway:

An LLM provides the intelligence, but the surrounding architecture gives an AI agent the ability to plan, remember, interact, execute, and complete tasks.

The future isn't just about building more powerful AI models.

It's about building reliable, scalable, and autonomous AI systems.

That's the real foundation of Agentic AI.
